name: Potassium
description: Potassium functions primarily as an osmotic regulator, enzyme activator, and stomatal controller without forming fixed organic compounds.
importance: Regulates plant water balance via stomatal aperture opening/closing, enhances drought hardiness, strengthens cell walls to prevent lodging, and improves grain/fruit quality and disease resistance.
deficiency_symptoms: Marginal scorching and necrosis starting on older leaf tips ('burnt edges'), weakened stalks, reduced resistance to drought and fungal infections.
excess_symptoms: High potassium concentrations in soil solution can antagonize uptake of magnesium (Mg) and calcium (Ca), resulting in grass tetany or calcium deficiency symptoms.
management_practices: Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP) or Sulfate of Potash (SOP) based on soil test calibration.
Split potassium applications in coarse-textured sandy soils to counter downward leaching losses.
Recycle crop residues (such as straw) back into the soil as plant residues are naturally rich in potassium.
